reason: First question list for the migration of the question system into the running instance. The node frontier records only what holds where; these questions ask what the object is like at the places where every method has become tight, and why. Each is grounded in published records read in the original, and conjectural parts are marked as such.

questions.statement: In every regime where the one-step difference b_{n,k}-b_{n,k-1} has been analysed, the decisive configurations are components (blocks, subtrees, prime blocks) whose size lies just above the capacity k, and the heavy-site mass they carry is of order k^(1/3) while the smooth background curvature stays O(1) - which is where the universal k^(-1/3) relative margin comes from. What is the local limit law of such a threshold-adjacent component (its size offset from k, its heavy-site count, its tie/blocked status, and its first finite-size correction), and is it one and the same object in the right bulk (the D_lambda cluster), the left second layer (the D_3 cluster), the central window (the two components whose deficits add to S), and the pole regime (prime blocks of size near k)? A sufficient answer gives one local law from which the regime-specific constants (2/I_0 at the center, m_3 on the second layer, the window deficit D(x-hat) on the right, the resonance depth at the pole) are recovered, or shows that these regimes involve genuinely different local objects.
questions.grounds: r9d97cea...: in the first (right) bulk the heavy sites split into a geometric part at the top (mass B_lambda) and a rare cluster of size k^(1/3) located within O(k^(2/3)) above the threshold with intensity D_lambda; k^(2/3)E[H_k] and k^(-1/3)E[(Z_k)_2] both tend to D_lambda I_0 (informal proof, review supported). r6b37c7e... sections 6.1-6.4: the convex-kink identity d = Conv - Kink shows the moment test measures two pieces of amplitude D I_0 k^(1/3) whose difference is the finite layer curvature, hence the k^(-1/3) margin; D_lambda equals the boundary flux of the layer profile; the ratio of threshold profiles between the second and first layer converges to D_3/D_lambda = 1.824 much faster than either profile converges, suggesting the slow finite-size correction lives in the local threshold structure (observation, binary64). rce3dc75... section 10: at the center the two compared terms share the leading constant and differ only at relative order (2/I)k^(-1/3). ra4c01fc... section 10.1: in the right window the finite-c margin falls short of its limit by D(x-hat)c^(-1/3), D about 5-9.5 (unverified numerics). r20df549... sections 3.5-3.6b and ra52a3c0... section 5: on the right half 92-95% of the blocked-maximum loss comes from chains descending to within 0.5k^(2/3) of k, and the gain/loss boundary r* ~ 0.63k^(1/3) is set by chains ending that close to the threshold (hazard lemma proved; r* law heuristic). rf451d83... section 3: at the pole, prime-block lengths concentrate in a boundary layer of width k/sigma_k around k, producing a period-k oscillation and a resonance trough at k*theta ~ 2*pi (observation). r1b79fab... section 6: in the central window d follows the density of S = X^(1)+X^(2), the sum of two components' deficits (weak-sense proof). The index module on maximum-tree chains, nested block paths and Borel bridges correctly insists that the global chains are different processes; this question asks whether the local structure at the threshold is nevertheless shared. Conjectural.

questions.statement: In the window t = (n-2k)/k^(2/3) around the center, independently measured landmarks fall close together: the peak of d = b_{n,k}-b_{n,k-1} at t* ~ 2.05 (the mode of f_S), the sign change of the chain excess X'' at ~2.09, the failure of the published bound K''(k) > J^G at t ~ 2.1-2.5 while d itself stays large and positive, the peak of the relative-second-difference profile at t ~ 2.59, and the maximum ~2.25 of the moment ratio R at t ~ 4; towards t -> 0 the capacity-response of the mean rises to 50-80% of E[Z]^2 and the margin of every method shrinks, while for t in a fixed interval [t_0, T] the moment margin stays O(1). What is the limiting structure of this window - the laws of d, mu, R and the response ratio rho as functions of t - and why does the reach of the one-heavy-block environment J^G coincide with the mode of f_S? A sufficient answer derives the window profiles from a two-component (or other) limit law, explains the coincidence of the landmarks or shows it to be accidental, and identifies the quantity that makes t -> 0 the tightest point for the central proof, the right-side proof, and the left-side moment tests alike.
questions.grounds: r1b79fab... section 6: f_S has mode t* = 2.0515 and the window profile of mu is f_S(t)/E(S-t)_+ with maximum at t ~ 2.59; conjecture LW states the pointwise window law; the review feedback (section 7) flags that the producer's d-peak at 2.09k^(2/3) sits at the same place as two quantities in r475ada... section 7 and that the common cause is an open question. r475ada... section 7: X'' becomes negative at nu ~ 2.09k^(2/3) and K''(k)-J^G at nu ~ 2.1-2.5k^(2/3), while d is positive and large there; the true-marker comparison K''(k) > J_n(k-1) holds everywhere measured with d to relative 10^(-4), so the loss lives entirely in replacing J by J^G (binary64 map, exact for small k). r6b37c7e... sections 5.4 and 6.6: the moment ratio R has a k-independent window profile with maximum ~2.25-2.27 at t ~ 4, tends to 1 as t -> 0 like (2/I_0)k^(-1/3), and the limit function of this profile was not derived. r10ff8c2... sections 5.5 and 5.7: the tightest point of the left moment window is its left end n = 2k+41; the exact identity T = E_k^2 + Delta_1 + Delta_2 shows the second-stage cancellation survives only in a boundary layer t < 0.5-1 where the capacity response of the mean reaches 0.5-0.8 of E^2, with the conjecture e' = e^2/2 for the limit profile. rce3dc75... section 10, r8a9b11e... section 3.3, ra4c01fc... section 10.3: the center is the tightest point of the central proof, of the right-side proof (limit ratio 1.795 at lambda = 1/2) and of the unfolded central method (eta = 1 hardest). All landmark values are binary64 observations; the coincidence is unexplained.

questions.statement: The one-step difference is a difference of two positive counts, b_{n,k}-b_{n,k-1} = 2E_{n,k} - B_{n,k-1} (even ties minus blocked maxima), of the same order and with relative gap of order k^(-1/3). On the right half the exact endpoint decomposition shows the sign by chain endpoint is -,+,-: chains ending within r* ~ 0.63k^(1/3) of the threshold lose (the threshold-child hazard stays O(1)), chains ending slightly further gain, shallow chains lose; the compensation happens between classes, not inside them, and every H-slice or site-wise comparison is negative somewhere. Where does the compensation live: what is the natural pairing or transport that carries blocked-maximum mass to tie mass, how close to a bijection must it be, and what replaces the chain-endpoint classes on the left half where the heavy vertices form a tree with side branches and H_k can exceed 1? A sufficient answer exhibits an explicit transport (or proves that no local one exists) that accounts for the sign geography on the right and gives its leaf-wise analogue on the left.
questions.grounds: r20df549... section 3: Theorem 3.1 (proved) splits b_{n,k}-b_{n,k-1} for k+1 <= n <= 2k-1 by chain endpoint; Lemma 3.2 (proved) gives the hazard h_pi(r) -> beta_r/(e - sum_{j<r} beta_j), equal to 1/e at r = 0; the three-stage sign and the widening loss band r* = 1, 4, 8, 13 (n = 600 ... 3*10^4, lambda = 0.7) are binary64 observations, with deep-class losses certified exactly at increasing positions (300,210), (600,420), (1000,700); section 7 lists inter-class transport and the left-half generalisation as open. ra52a3c0... section 6: slicing by H shows the h >= 1 slices negative well before the mode (the review corrects the n = 25 figure to the h = 1 slice), so positivity is a global compensation and site-wise or H-wise injections are impossible. r475ada... section 7: on the left the loss is entirely in B <= J^G, and beyond the band the right comparison is 'excess of K'' versus excess of B', two negative quantities that nearly cancel. r9d97cea... section 8.2: for n > 2k heavy sites acquire active side branches; the restricted response has an exact recursion (Theorem R1) but its asymptotics are open. r20df549... section 5.1: the relative gap is n^(-1/3) (published profile h_cmp), so any pairing must be asymptotically almost bijective. The transport itself is conjectural.

questions.statement: The left half is organised by the number r ~ n/k of components above capacity: fixed-ratio profiles Phi_r with internal minima of Phi_r''/Phi_r, moment statistics that oscillate in n with period about k, mu-monotonicity breaking inside each layer because the layer sits between a 'block is born' and a 'block disappears' threshold, and in the pole regime n >> k^(3/2) the same period-k structure reappearing as the second zero pair of the prime-block renewal. How do the layer constants - curvature kappa_r = lambda^2 Phi_r''/Phi_r, boundary flux D_r, and the moment-margin constant m_r = kappa_r/(D_r I_0) - behave for r >= 4 and uniformly as r grows with k, and how does the layer description hand over to the renewal description with slope kappa_k and threshold density P_k(infinity)? A sufficient answer gives formulas or asymptotics for kappa_r, D_r, m_r valid uniformly in r, matched to the pole-regime quantities, or shows that the hand-over is not uniform and where it breaks.
questions.grounds: r24b9bf1...: fixed-hierarchy profiles Phi_r and their convexity are established, but the record states (section 5) that its monotone-density argument does not give the exact second-difference limit. r1b79fab... section 5: M_r = Phi_r''/Phi_r has internal minima at lambda*_2 = 0.6435, lambda*_3 = 0.4240, lambda*_4 ~ 0.308 (the last numerical), and the mechanism is the two thresholds at the ends of each layer (sections 5.3, 10). r6b37c7e... sections 6.3-6.5 and 6.8: kappa_3, D_3, m_3 computed for the second layer, m_3 minimum ~15.34 at n/k ~ 2.55, exact end-of-layer constants 9/(8I_0) and 1/(3I_0), an end-of-layer exponent rule, and the explicit statement that higher layers and layer number growing with k were not treated (conjecture 6.3 for the second layer; the first-layer version is the informal theorem of r9d97cea...). r10ff8c2... section 5.4: E_n, T_n and P_k(n) oscillate in n with period about k and T_n decreases on long intervals, so n-monotonicity reductions are false; section 5.3: with the true mean the first-moment test holds from n_J ~ 2.1k-3.6k, so the upper window is in principle a matter of a mean lower bound and a threshold-density upper bound. rf451d83... sections 3.2-3.3: at the pole the renewal sequence oscillates with period about k through a second zero pair whose gap delta* sigma_k^2 = 33-47 is still far from the asymptotic 2*pi^2 at k <= 10^5 (observation). r9d97cea... section 8.2: on the left the logarithmic growth of E[Z] sits entirely in the cell j/k in [1, 1.25) and the mean matches the one-pole formula (N/k)kappa_k - 1 (binary64). Mostly observation and conjecture; Phi_r convexity is proved.

questions.statement: The right half (n < 2k) is now informally proved and the left half (n > 2k) is what remains of the root. At the center the two sides differ structurally: the first-layer profile Phi_2 vanishes linearly at lambda = 1/2 so the moment-margin constant stays finite (2/I_0), whereas the second-layer profile Phi_3 diverges like delta^(-1/2) and the constant grows like 1.198/delta; on the right the vertices of size > k form a single chain with H_k <= 1 and the proof could sum over the start row and reverse time to turn conditioned bridges into an unconditioned killed Borel walk, whereas on the left they form a tree with side branches, H_k can exceed 1, and the one-heavy-block environment fails at nu ~ 2.5k^(2/3). Which structural property of left-half configurations - the second component above capacity, the side branches, or something else - is responsible for the extra difficulty, and does the right-side device (unconditioning by time reversal, absorption of the top row) have a left-half analogue? A sufficient answer identifies the responsible structure and either gives a left-half representation with the same unconditioning effect or an argument why none exists.
questions.grounds: r6b37c7e... section 6.5: proved endpoint constants show m_3 diverges at both ends of the second layer while the first-layer constant m(1/2+) = 2/I_0 is finite, with the asymmetry traced to Phi_2 vanishing linearly and Phi_3 growing like delta^(-1/2) at the center. r8a9b11e... sections 3.2-3.3, 4.2-4.4, 7: the right-side proof succeeds by absorbing the top row, setting alpha = 0, and the time-reversal identity RW; the center is its tightest point (limit ratio 1.795) and the record lists row-wise bridge variance as the obstacle that reversal bypassed. r20df549... section 7: on the left the heavy vertices form a tree, so the endpoint decomposition must become a leaf-wise decomposition; not attempted. r9d97cea... section 8.2: side branches appear for n > 2k and the restricted response's asymptotics are open. r5f5cf73... section 4: the central Gaussian method unfolds over the entire right half because t = 1 is a critical point for every n; no left analogue is stated. r475ada... section 7: the published left bound fails at nu ~ 2.1-2.5k^(2/3) only because the restricted environment is replaced by a one-heavy-block environment. This question differs from op-tie-block-transport (which asks for the pairing) and op-layer-period (which asks for the layer constants): it asks what structural feature separates the two halves. Interpretive; conjectural.

questions.statement: In the right critical window the two positive counts in b_{n,k}-b_{n,k-1} = 2E_{n,k}-B_{n,k-1} have universal limits, and numerically (2E - B)/(2 pi) = -f' where f is the limit density of the normalised deficit: the slope of the critical density is 'two-car tie density minus blocked-maximum density', and the mode x_* = 0.5996 is where the two densities balance. What events of the Brownian running-maximum process R and its area functional Lambda correspond to 'two cars tie at the maximum' and 'the maximum is blocked by capacity', so that the identity and the mode-constant limits follow from the continuum law rather than from numerics? A sufficient answer proves the identity by identifying E and B (and the threshold sites with the increments dR) as functionals of (R, Lambda), and says what the same continuum reading gives in the central window where two components contribute.
questions.grounds: ra4c01fc... section 9: the window limit functions E-hat and B-hat (Theorem C, informal outline) have margin 2E/B - 1 vanishing at x-hat_0 = 0.59963, equal to the published mode constant x_* to four digits, and the peer verified (2E - B)/(2 pi) = -f' at ten points to relative 10^(-10) to 10^(-12) without proving it. r1b79fab... section 8: from the published third-order local limits, c^(4/3)(V - B)/p_n -> -f', so Theorem C is equivalent to four-or-more ties being negligible on the window scale; the Mills ratio of X governs the second differences of A/b there. ra52a3c0... section 4.3b: identifying threshold sites with the increments dR and using the Brownian functions h_j, q_j reproduces the mode constants (lim epsilon_c = -0.29710, lim E[Z_c H_c] = 0.44299, lim F_c = 0.14589) that the measured values approach monotonically; the identification steps are unproven. r5f5cf73... section 2.2: the sign change of 2E2 - B tracks the row mode to second order, m + c_1 n^(-1/3) with c_1 = 1.2485, and the node X holds exactly where the row increases. Glossary entries H_S (r0dc57fa...) and H_C (r3e8c952...) are the existing continuum functions for the boundary comparisons and should be reconciled with E, B. The continuum identification is conjectural.

questions.statement: Unimodality of the maximum-displacement row has been found to fail under many deformations of the original object: fixing the outcome permutation (non-unimodal fibres for every n >= 7), weighting the tail coordinate by a power r^a with 2 < a < a_* ~ 2.5748 (eventually non-unimodal rows), and giving n cars n+r-1 spaces (log-concavity on the decreasing side fails for all n >= 7 and r >= 64 n^3), while the power-weighted limit density x^r f_X stays unimodal exactly for -1/2 < r < 5/2. What is the boundary of unimodality under such deformations, and what structural feature of the original model does each failure remove - saturation of independent displacement intervals in a fibre, the log-convex Cayley weight of a sparse collision component, the polynomial tail of X? A sufficient answer gives a unified account of which deformations preserve the single sign change and why, thereby saying what property of the original n-car, n-space process the statement P is really about.
questions.grounds: r81e7051...: for every n >= 7 there is a non-unimodal outcome-permutation fibre (sigma = (1,2,3,5,4,6,7) gives 222 > 216 < 264 while b_7 is unimodal); the obstacle is named saturation of the independent displacement intervals; the peer proved x^r f_X strictly unimodal for -1/2 < r < 5/2; log-concavity of the full row fails for all sufficiently large n because of the polynomial tail of X (review supported). r7eeaca03...: the peer extended the eventual non-unimodality of power-weighted finite rows to the exact range 2 < a < a_* ~ 2.57480775688, and gave the exact n = 304 dip that refutes the log-tail-coordinate strengthening (review supported). rd4015a8...: Theorem C proves that with n cars and n+r-1 spaces the decreasing-side log-concavity fails for all n >= 7, r >= 64 n^3, with the exact example n = 7, r = 63; the explanation is that a sparse single-collision component with log-convex Cayley weights dominates, and the record states that the original n spaces are not in this sparse regime, so nothing transfers to the original P (review supported). The index lists further deformations (lucky-car weights, fixed-preference orbits, total-displacement tilts) whose failures I did not read in the original. The unifying account is conjectural.
